subject: Recap: FinHealth private VPC/on-prem discovery — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Recap: FinHealth private VPC/on-prem discovery — next steps

Hi Liam —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Summary of pain points you shared:
- Regulated workloads (PHI) — cannot send model inputs to public hosted endpoints.
- Need strong KMS/HSM integration and customer-managed keys (BYOK) for encryption at rest and in-transit.
- Some sites operate in an air-gapped/isolated environment for processing sensitive records.
- Tight audit/compliance needs (retention, detailed request logs, SOC2 evidence).
- Current infra is AWS (EKS, internal NLB), team prefers VPC-based connectivity or on-prem options.

Current stack you described:
- AWS (EKS, private subnets), in-house key management tied to AWS KMS and a vendor HSM.
- Existing ML infra: in-house inference for some non-sensitive workloads; looking to offload LLM inference for scale and maintenance.

Success criteria you mentioned:
1) No egress of PHI outside FinHealth-controlled network (private VPC or on-prem).
2) Ability to integrate with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and PKCS#11 where applicable.
3) Detailed audit logs+SLA for latency/availability for core inference paths.
4) Deployment options: VPC peering/PrivateLink for cloud, and an air-gapped on-prem package for isolated sites.

What Redwood can offer (high level):
- Private deployment (VPC) with customer-managed networking and optional private control plane.
- KMS/HSM integrations and support for BYOK workflows; we can support PKCS#11/HSM proxies for air-gapped sites.
- Audit logs, request tracing, and optional extended retention for compliance needs.
- On-prem install artifact for fully air-gapped environments (we'll need to validate that against your ops processes).

Immediate next steps:
- I'll share our Private deployment checklist and a SOC2 summary (attached) for your security team to review.
- Schedule a technical deep dive with your infra/security folks + our solutions engineer (propose Dec 3, 10:00 AM PT) — need to discuss VPC connectivity options, egress rules, and KMS/HSM specifics.
- Please send an architecture diagram or network constraints doc to help our SREs scope the on-prem/air-gap work.

Attachments: redwood-private-reqs-checklist.pdf; SOC2-TypeII-summary-2025.pdf; proposed-tech-deep-dive.ics

If that summary looks right, I can get the technical invite out and loop in Dylan (our SE) and Aditya (sales lead).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Redwood Inference — Production-grade LLM inference across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments

Marissa — thanks for the tidy recap, that matches our notes. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Security contact for the deep dive will be Samantha Reed (samantha.reed@finhealth.com) — she'll own the KMS/HSM review.
- We do have a handful of processing sites that are fully air-gapped; timeline for those is Q1 2027 procurement and pilot.
- Budget band is roughly mid-six figures for year-one committed spend if the solution meets the BYOK + compliance requirements.

Action items for us: we'll circulate a high-level network diagram internally and get Samantha's availability for the Dec 3 slot.

Appreciate it — looking forward to the tech session.

— Liam

liam@finhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finhealth.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: FinHealth private VPC/on-prem discovery — next steps

Thanks Liam — looping in Dylan (SE) and Aditya (sales lead) to coordinate the tech deep dive and security artifact review.

Dylan/Aditya — attaching the checklist and SOC2 summary from my earlier note. Key asks from FinHealth:
- Confirm we can support private VPC connectivity (PrivateLink or VPC peering) without egressing PHI to public endpoints.
- KMS/BYOK integration details: FinHealth uses AWS KMS + vendor HSM; they may require PKCS#11 for the on-prem sites.
- Air-gap option: they will need an installable artifact and a secure process for exchanging signed binaries/containers.

Liam — can you share the high-level network diagram and any constraints on outbound ports (e.g., 443 only via proxy), and confirm whether your HSM exposes a PKCS#11 interface or sits behind a vendor appliance?

If Dec 3 10:00 AM PT works for Samantha, I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda: 1) connectivity options + network constraints, 2) KMS/HSM integration patterns, 3) air-gap/on-prem install requirements, 4) timelines & next milestones.

Marissa
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@finhealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Recap: FinHealth private VPC/on-prem discovery — next steps

Hi Liam / Marissa — quick technical clarifications ahead of the deep dive: 

- For private deployments we support PrivateLink, VPC peering, and an on-prem air-gapped package. For VPC options we typically require a NAT or proxy for image pulls during initial setup; for fully air-gapped installs we provide an offline bundle and signed checksums.
- KMS/HSM: we support AWS KMS CMKs and have worked with PKCS#11-backed HSMs. To confirm integration surface: does FinHealth expect Redwood to hold only a pointer to the key (BYOK) or for calls to be proxied to your HSM? Both are possible but the latter requires network reachability to the HSM or an HSM proxy.
- Audit/logs: we can provide per-request logs and request IDs; please indicate retention window you need (30/90/365 days).

Proposed agenda item for the deep dive: a short demo of our VPC connectivity options + sample KMS integration flow. Dec 3, 10:00 AM PT works for me; happy to move if that doesn't match Samantha's calendar.

Thanks — Dylan
